policy: medical if ANY part of the message describes a physical symptom or a change in the body (pain, bleeding, leaking fluid, swelling, fever, headache, the baby moving less), asks about a medication or supplement, describes a mental-health concern beyond ordinary nerves (hopelessness, panic that won't stop, not sleeping for days, not wanting to be here, thoughts of harming herself or the baby), or asks whether something about the pregnancy, birth, recovery or the baby's health is normal or safe — even when the rest of the message is about scheduling or coverage. Ordinary worries and feelings, and logistics (scheduling, coverage, paperwork, what to pack, birth preferences, feeding routines with no health problem) are non-medical.
